label: LTX-2.3 two-stage T2V
prompt: A cat and a dog baking a cake together in a kitchen.

b300-cfg-parallel-bcg.description: B300: The default command plus breakable CUDA graphs (LTX-2/2.3 are on sglang's validated BCG list), captured at the case shape.
b300-cfg-parallel-bcg.notes: TRT-LLM's LTX-2 row runs CUDA graphs (NVIDIA's official config) at 0.044 s per stage-1 step against sglang's 0.192 s (4xB300, 2026-10-22); stage 1 is ~1.5k tokens, so the step is launch-bound. BCG replays the same kernels, so the output is unchanged. Promoted from cand-bcg by the 2026-10-22 4xB300 A/B (scripts/run_b300_ab_20261022.sh, second wave): two rounds, 4.735/4.726 s against default (eager) 6.294/6.202, cand-usp2-bcg 5.420/5.435, cand-usp2 8.79/9.13.

default.description: Fallback SGLang command when no hardware-specific profile matches.
default.notes: Use hardware-specific profiles for formal H100/H200 runs.

h100-80gb-2gpu.description: Cookbook-aligned H100 80GB command for the LTX2.3 two-stage 121-frame case.
h100-80gb-2gpu.notes: Snapshot mode avoids H100 resident VRAM pressure. DEAD AGAINST CURRENT SGLANG (checked 2026-09-13): `--ltx2-two-stage-device-mode snapshot` is rejected by the parser -- the choices are now 'original' and 'resident', so `snapshot` was retired upstream. Not guessing a replacement: 'resident' keeps components on the GPU and this profile exists for an 80GB card, so the substitution has to be measured on H100 rather than picked. Not selected on Blackwell (b200 takes `default`, which does not pass the flag at all), so it has not affected any B200 run. Catch this class with scripts/validate_serve_args.py, which found it.
h100-80gb-2gpu.policy_exception: Measured H100 A/B 2026-07-03 (steady-state single_e2e): speed+compile OOMs on 2x80GB (79.1/79.2 GiB used, 30MiB alloc failure during request) — two-stage residency + compile workspace does not fit. Snapshot device mode is the fastest configuration that fits (12.03s).

h200-2gpu.description: Cookbook-aligned H200 command for the LTX2.3 two-stage 121-frame case.
h200-2gpu.notes: Resident mode is the fastest LTX2.3 two-stage path when both DiTs fit in VRAM.

official-original-2gpu.description: Official stage-switching semantics profile for LTX2.3 two-stage comparisons.
official-original-2gpu.notes: Use this only when official switching semantics are more important than latency.

cand-bcg.description: The default command plus breakable CUDA graphs (LTX-2/2.3 are on sglang's validated BCG list), captured at the case shape. Never selected on its own: A/B arm.
cand-bcg.notes: TRT-LLM's LTX-2 row runs CUDA graphs (NVIDIA's official config) at 0.044 s per stage-1 step against sglang's 0.192 s (4xB300, 2026-10-22); stage 1 is ~1.5k tokens, so the step is launch-bound. BCG replays the same kernels, so the output is unchanged. VALIDATION PENDING (4xB300 A/B).

cand-usp2.description: Ulysses 2 across both stages instead of CFG parallel: stage 2 has no CFG, so under CFG parallel it runs on the main rank alone (LTX2RefinementStage is MAIN_RANK_ONLY). Never selected on its own: A/B arm.
cand-usp2.notes: TRT-LLM switches stage 2 from cfg2 to Ulysses 2 ('there is no cfg in stage 2'). Same math, different placement. VALIDATION PENDING (4xB300 A/B).

cand-usp2-bcg.description: cand-usp2 plus breakable CUDA graphs at the case shape. Never selected on its own: A/B arm.
cand-usp2-bcg.notes: TRT-LLM switches stage 2 from cfg2 to Ulysses 2 ('there is no cfg in stage 2'). Same math, different placement. VALIDATION PENDING (4xB300 A/B).

vllm-omni.model_override_reason: vLLM-Omni loads LTX-2.3 only from the Diffusers conversion of the official weights (its recipe: 'LTX-2.3 requires the Diffusers checkpoint; the raw Lightricks/LTX-2.3 safetensors repository is not directly loadable'); the two-stage upsampler and distilled LoRA still come from Lightricks/LTX-2.3.

blackwell-2gpu-twostage-cfg.description: Blackwell: ordinary LTX-2.3 two-stage with guidance parallel 2 (two of stage 1's four passes per rank), cuDNN attention.
blackwell-2gpu-twostage-cfg.notes: Stage 1 runs the official LTX-2.3 guider by default (video CFG 3 / audio CFG 7, STG 1.0 on block 28, modality 3, rescale 0.7: four transformer passes a step), the same values as sglang's LTX23SamplingParams; the request pins them in extra_params and omits the top-level guidance_scale, which vLLM-Omni applies to BOTH CFG fields after extra_params (audio CFG 7 would become 3). Default negative prompt is the ltx-pipelines one in both. VALIDATION PENDING (round 2026-10-22, 4xB300).

default.description: Ordinary LTX-2.3 two-stage with guidance parallel 2.
default.notes: As blackwell-2gpu-twostage-cfg with FLASH_ATTN (Hopper). Not measured yet.

cand-vaepp.description: VAE patch parallel 2 (tiled decode on both GPUs). Never selected on its own: A/B arm.
cand-vaepp.notes: Derived from `blackwell-2gpu-twostage-cfg` (the profile B300 selects). Audit 2026-10-23 (image finding 4, LTX sub-audit): vLLM-Omni decodes on one GPU, although its features matrix lists VAE patch parallel (decode) for LTX-2 and LTX-2.3 (docs/user_guide/diffusion_features.md; tile mode, the flag's default); TRT-LLM (parallel_vae 2) and sglang decode on two. Estimated 0.1-0.2 s. VALIDATION PENDING (wave 4, 4xB300).

lightx2v.reason: LightX2V cannot run the official LTX-2.3 two-stage workload: one transformer serves both stages with any LoRA merged at load (ltx2_runner.py at 19c19614), and the profile it had never enabled the upsampler, so every earlier row was one stage at the full 768x512 -- heavier than sglang's two-stage, never comparable. Audited 2026-10-22.

h100.reason: OOM on H100 80GB: LTX-2.3 22B two-stage 121-frame t2av peak exceeds 80GB even with every lossless lever (seq_p_size=2 activation sharding + block cpu_offload + Gemma/VAE offload + exact flash_attn3). Upstream profiles target H200 141GB. command_profiles carry the best-attempted lossless H100 config for provenance.

default.description: LightX2V upstream LTX-2.3 t2av path for the LTX-2.3 121-frame case.
default.notes: Uses upstream LTX-2.3 audio-video runner. CFG parallel is not enabled because upstream mm_guider and cfg_parallel are not compatible. Also what Blackwell selects: no B200 profile has been validated for this case yet, so the fallback is the upstream single-GPU path.

h200-2gpu-tp.description: H200 same-GPU LightX2V LTX-2.3 t2av tensor-parallel command/config.
h200-2gpu-tp.notes: Use tensor parallelism for same-GPU comparison because upstream mm_guider raises when combined with cfg_parallel.

h200-1gpu.notes: Single-GPU profile follows current upstream LTX-2.3 scripts; no cache, torch compile, or quantized model path.

h100-2gpu-sp.description: H100 LightX2V LTX-2.3 t2av: lossless flash_attn3 + sequence parallelism (seq_p_size=2) to shard the 121-frame video activations across 2 GPUs. TP shards weights but the OOM is activation-bound, so SP is the right lever.
h100-2gpu-sp.notes: Best-attempted lossless H100 config (seq_p_size=2 + block cpu_offload + Gemma/VAE offload + flash_attn3). Still OOMs at a later stage on 80GB — LTX-2.3 t2av needs H200. Kept for provenance; result is OOM on H100.

trtllm-visual.reason: TensorRT-LLM 1.4.0rc1 has no LTX-2.3: LTX2Pipeline lists only Lightricks/LTX-2 (19B), and '2.3' appears in no hf_id, config, test or supported-models table (checked 2026-10-22).

comfyui.reason: ComfyUI loads LTX-2.3, but no official workflow reproduces this case: sglang runs LTX-2.3's multimodal guidance in stage 1 (video CFG 3 + STG 1.0 on block 28 + modality 3, audio CFG 7 + STG + modality -- up to four DiT passes per step, LTX23SamplingParams), while ComfyUI's LTX-2.3 T2V template (and the LTX-2.5 one) is the distilled-LoRA fast path at cfg 1. A graph built from LTXVSpatioTemporalGuidance / LTXVModalityGuidance / LTXVDualCFGGuider could match it but has no upstream reference and is not validated.

fastvideo.reason: FastVideo main (2b164405c3d1, 2026-10-07) registers LTX-2.3, but this harness integrates FastVideo for MiniMax-H3 only (2026-10-08); no command validated.

sglang.negative_prompt: blurry, out of focus, overexposed, underexposed, low contrast, washed out colors, excessive noise, grainy texture, poor lighting, flickering, motion blur, distorted proportions, unnatural skin tones, deformed facial features, asymmetrical face, missing facial features, extra limbs, disfigured hands, wrong hand count, artifacts around text, inconsistent perspective, camera shake, incorrect depth of field, background too sharp, background clutter, distracting reflections, harsh shadows, inconsistent lighting direction, color banding, cartoonish rendering, 3D CGI look, unrealistic materials, uncanny valley effect, incorrect ethnicity, wrong gender, exaggerated expressions, wrong gaze direction, mismatched lip sync, silent or muted audio, distorted voice, robotic voice, echo, background noise, off-sync audio, incorrect dialogue, added dialogue, repetitive speech, jittery movement, awkward pauses, incorrect timing, unnatural transitions, inconsistent framing, tilted camera, flat lighting, inconsistent tone, cinematic oversaturation, stylized filters, or AI artifacts.

_note: sglang's request carries its own default negative prompt explicitly (2026-10-23; byte-identical to LTX2SamplingParams.negative_prompt at sglang 82f7249c, the LTX-2 case's negative_prompt), so the harness can tag it per request like every negative it sends: left to the server default, it was one constant text that sglang's conditioning cache encoded once per server (text_encoding.get_or_compute_negative_text_embedding), while the competitors re-encode theirs.
